   Motorcyclist, pillion rider die after Tampines accident; search ongoing for pair who fled
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 In photos of the accident in Tampines circulating on social media, various vehicles can be seen in severely damaged states.
 PHOTOS: SGROAD BLOCKS/TRAFFIC NEWS/TELEGRAM, ST READER
 Ann Neo
 Published   Oct 30, 2026, 09:51 AM
 Updated   Oct 30, 2026, 04:57 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise 中文 Two people died after a late-night Tampines crash involving two cars and a motorcycle. Police and SCDF were alerted at about 10.35pm on Oct 29.
 A 24-year-old motorcyclist and his 24-year-old pillion rider died in hospital. A 25-year-old female car driver was also taken to hospital.
 Police are searching for the male driver and female passenger of the second car, who fled before officers arrived. Investigations continue, as road accidents and motorcycle deaths have risen.
 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – Two people were killed after a multi-vehicle accident late on Oct 29 in Tampines, while a search is under way for two others who had fled the scene before the authorities arrived.
 In a media reply on Oct 30, the police and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) said they were alerted to an accident involving two cars and a motorcycle in Tampines Avenue 12 at around 10.35pm the day before.
 A 24-year-old male motorcyclist and his 24-year-old female pillion rider were taken unconscious to hospital, where they subsequently died.
 The police added that a 25-year-old female driver of one of the cars involved was taken conscious to hospital.
 SCDF said two people were taken to Changi General Hospital and one person to Sengkang General Hospital.
 Meanwhile, a search is under way for the male driver and the female passenger of the second car, who were not at the scene when police officers arrived.
 Preliminary probes revealed that the pair had left the scene after the accident, the police said.
 Investigations are ongoing.
 Eyewitnesses recount moments after crash
 An eyewitness, who gave her name only as Syazwani, was just metres behind the motorcyclist and his pillion rider when the crash happened.
 Speaking to The Straits Times on Oct 30, the 31-year-old said: “We heard a loud screech, and then we saw a blue Audi that was travelling in the opposite direction crash through the railings. There were some sparks.”
 She added that the car had hit the motorcycle first, with the impact sending the motorcyclist and his pillion rider flying through the air, before hitting another black car.
 Debris from the vehicles, uprooted vegetation and what appears to be broken pieces of road dividers were strewn across the area.
 PHOTOS: SGROAD BLOCKS/TRAFFIC NEWS/TELEGRAM, ST READER
 Syazwani was heading home on her motorcycle at the time, with her 36-year-old friend Natassja on a separate motorcycle just behind her.
 Both women, who work in the food and beverage sector, immediately pulled over to help.
 Syazwani said that when she walked towards the blue Audi, she saw a man unbuckling his seatbelt and hopping out of the vehicle. He did not appear to be injured, she added.
 Next to him was a woman who also appeared uninjured, she said, though she looked shaken and was unable to walk.
 “The guy had to drag her up by the armpits,” she said, adding that loud music was still playing inside the car after the crash.
 Seeing that the pair appeared physically fine, Syazwani left them to check on the others.
 The last time she turned to look at them, they were stumbling away from the road towards a grass patch, she said.
 She added that when she got to the black car, the woman behind the wheel was conscious but appeared shaken and seemed to be injured at the hips.
 Both the motorcyclist and his pillion rider were already unresponsive by the time she got to them less than a minute after the accident happened, she said. They were lying face down on the ground.
 Natassja told ST that she called the ambulance while Syazwani assessed the situation.
 Multiple SCDF vehicles and personnel arrived at the scene within minutes.
 “When the ambulance arrived, that’s when we realised the man and the woman in the blue Audi were no longer at the scene, and they had run away,” Natassja said.
 “There were joggers around us. They tried to find the pair, but were unable to,” she said.
 Eyewitnesses said the blue car collided with a motorcycle and another black car, before overturning on its side.
 PHOTOS: NATASSJA
 Scattered debris, uprooted vegetation litter the area
 Photos and videos of the aftermath of the accident circulating on social media show the vehicles in severely damaged states.
 One blue car can be seen overturned on its side among the shrubs, with its rear heavily crushed. A tree and a pole appeared to have been knocked down, spilling onto an adjacent pedestrian walkway.
 A second black car was on a grass patch, with its rear bumper and licence plate dislodged.
 A third vehicle, the motorcycle, lay heavily mangled on the road, bearing severe chassis deformation.
 Debris from the vehicles, uprooted vegetation and what appeared to be broken pieces of road dividers were strewn across the area.
 Multiple SCDF vehicles and personnel can be seen at the scene.
 The fatal crash comes amid a broader rise in road accidents. 
 Traffic accidents resulting in injuries rose from 3,748 in the first half of 2025 to 3,869 in the same period in 2026, while the number of injured people increased from 4,894 to 5,090.
 Motorcyclists and pillion riders were involved in more than half, or 55.6%, of all traffic accidents in that same period.
 They continue to be the largest group of road users involved in fatal accidents, accounting for 45.9% of all road deaths in the first half of 2026.
